title: Factors Driving Government's Upward Revision of 2021 GDP Growth to 6% to 7%
what_it_is: Factors Driving Government's Upward Revision of 2021 GDP Growth to 6% to 7%

sections.label: MTI 2021 growth projection
sections.summary: In August, MTI projected the Singapore economy would expand by 6% to 7% in 2021, taking into account several developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: In August, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) projected that the Singapore economy would expand by 6% to 7% in 2021, taking into account several developments.

sections.label: First half GDP growth
sections.summary: Singapore's GDP grew 7.7% year-on-year in the first half, with manufacturing up 14.5% and finance and insurance up 7.4%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Two, Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the first half of the year came in at a better-than-expected 7.7% on a year-on-year basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: In particular, the outward-oriented sectors continued to grow strongly, with the manufacturing and finance and insurance sectors achieving growth of 14.5% and 7.4% respectively during this period.

sections.label: 2022 recovery and forecast
sections.summary: MTI expects the Singapore economy to continue recovering in 2022 and will announce the 2022 GDP growth forecast in November 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Looking ahead to 2022, MTI expects the Singapore economy to continue to recover as global growth is projected to remain positive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: MTI will announce Singapore's 2022 GDP growth forecast in November 2021.
